title: Measuring Inductive Biases of In-Context Learning with Underspecified Demonstrations
measurement_description: Measurement of feature bias in in-context learning for toxicity classification, specifically evaluating whether models predict labels based on whether a comment targets 'Muslim' or 'Christian/Jewish' people as an alternative feature to overall 'toxicity'.
findings: In the toxicity classification task, models (DAVINCI and TEXT-DAVINCI-002) did not exhibit a strong baseline feature bias towards the 'religion' feature (Muslim vs. Christian/Jewish) compared to 'toxicity'. When interventions were applied to steer the model towards the 'religion' feature (h2), they were generally successful, especially for TEXT-DAVINCI-002, which already showed a slight preference for the religion feature in the baseline, leading to substantial increases in h2-accuracy.
